ai-at-work.title: Europe is pushing back on Washington’s chip war
ai-at-work.excerpt: As ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet told TechCrunch in May, what China can currently buy are older-generation deep ultraviolet tools — gear first shipped about a decade ago — the same machines the MATCH Ac
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Europe is resisting US export restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment, arguing that blocking sales of decade-old chip tools to China is economically counterproductive and technically obsolete as a control measure. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because semiconductor supply chain instability directly impacts hardware availability, cloud infrastructure costs, and ultimately the tools and systems your organization depends on. Here's the thing: if Washington and Brussels can't get on the same page about what actually constitutes advanced technology, we're all going to be stuck explaining procurement delays to executives for years.

ai-at-work.title: AI researchers continue to leave Google for its rivals
ai-at-work.excerpt: Top AI researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel are leaving Google for Anthropic, following departures from top scientists Noam Shazeer and John Jumper.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google is losing its AI talent pipeline to competitors like Anthropic, with senior researchers like Adler and Pritzel walking out the door. For digital workplace leaders, this signals that compensation, prestige, and even ping-pong tables aren't enough to keep your best people if they feel constrained or undervalued. Google built its talent moat on "we have the smartest people," so watching that narrative crack is the corporate equivalent of finding out your secret sauce is just ketchup.

ai-at-work.title: Companies are scrambling to stop employees from maxing out AI budgets with small tasks
ai-at-work.excerpt: The tokenmaxxing era was brief. We now appear to be entering the era of token rationing.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are discovering that employees are burning through AI token budgets on trivial tasks instead of high-value work, forcing them to implement spending controls and usage policies. This matters because it reveals a fundamental problem with how organizations are rolling out AI tools: they're not thinking through governance, training, or actual use cases before handing out access. The irony is thick here. We spent decades teaching people that cloud storage is unlimited, then act shocked when they treat AI tokens the same way.

ai-at-work.title: Ornn raises $33M to help companies buy and sell AI compute as a commodity like oil
ai-at-work.excerpt: Artificial intelligence startup Ornn AI Inc. made a big splash today as it raised $33 million in seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz’s crypto-focused fund and others to build out a marketplace for c
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Ornn AI just raised $33 million to create a marketplace where companies can buy and sell AI compute power like a commodity. For digital workplace folks, this matters because it could eventually make AI tools cheaper and more accessible, which means better tools and fewer excuses from IT about why you can't have nice things. That said, I've seen plenty of "democratize the infrastructure" plays come and go, so let's wait and see if this actually changes pricing or just creates another middleman layer.

tools-tech.title: 12 rules of agentic AI for successful enterprise transformation
tools-tech.excerpt: Most AI pilots focus on capability and speed - and skip the hard work of earning trust from the business.
tools-tech.dwp_take: ZDNet published a piece about 12 rules for deploying agentic AI in enterprises, highlighting that most AI pilots chase speed and capability while neglecting the trust-building work that actually matters. This matters because digital workplace leaders are the ones caught between IT's AI excitement and end users' legitimate skepticism, so understanding trust mechanics beats understanding another AI framework. Here's the thing: I've watched 30 years of tech rollouts, and the pattern never changes. You can have the fanciest AI agent in the world, but if your employees don't trust it with their actual work, you've built an expensive paperweight.

tools-tech.title: Anthropic’s Claude Tag aims to turn workplace AI from a personal assistant into a teammate
tools-tech.excerpt: Claude Tag is Anthropic’s latest attempt at getting Claude out of your DMs and into your team’s Slack channels. AI assistants are increasingly showing up in the workplace to perform research, coding,
tools-tech.dwp_take: Anthropic just rolled out Claude Tag, a feature designed to move Claude from one-on-one chats into shared team spaces like Slack where the work actually happens. This matters because right now most workplace AI lives in silos, meaning each person gets their own answers and nobody benefits from what others discovered. Honestly, this is overdue, but let's see if teams actually use it or if it just becomes another bot cluttering the channel while everyone ignores it.

digital-culture.title: Qualcomm Buys Buzzy Chip Startup Modular for Nearly $4 Billion
digital-culture.excerpt: Modular, one of the most promising chip software startups of the AI era, heads for a multibillion-dollar exit.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Qualcomm just dropped nearly four billion dollars to acquire Modular, a startup that builds compiler software for AI chips. This matters because the tools companies use to run AI on their hardware directly impact how fast your workplace AI tools actually perform, from search to content generation to analytics. Here's the thing though: another AI startup gets swallowed by a mega-corp and suddenly all those promises about "open innovation" start sounding hollow. Let's see if Qualcomm actually ships what Modular promised or if this becomes vaporware with better funding.

industry-news.title: Zoom, Salesforce, Dialpad, and Others Bet Big on Agentic AI for CX
industry-news.excerpt: CCW showed agentic AI moving deeper into CX platforms. Here’s what IT leaders should know about governance, data, workforce planning, and rollout. The post Zoom, Salesforce, Dialpad, and Others Bet Bi
industry-news.dwp_take: Zoom, Salesforce, Dialpad and other major platforms are embedding agentic AI agents directly into customer experience tools to automate support workflows. This matters because IT leaders now need to think seriously about governance frameworks, data security, and how their support teams will actually work alongside these autonomous systems. The funny part is we're about to discover which companies built solid foundations for this and which ones are about to learn expensive lessons about deploying AI without a real plan.

industry-news.title: Healthcare Vendor Xsolis Reports Breach Affecting 1.4M People
industry-news.excerpt: Xsolis confirmed a healthcare data breach affecting nearly 1.4 million people after a phishing attack exposed health and identity data. The post Healthcare Vendor Xsolis Reports Breach Affecting 1.4M
industry-news.dwp_take: A healthcare vendor called Xsolis got hit by a phishing attack that exposed health and identity data for 1.4 million people. This matters because if your organization uses Xsolis or similar healthcare platforms, you're probably fielding breach notification emails right now and dealing with mandatory disclosure requirements across multiple states. The real kicker is that phishing still works in 2024, which means your security awareness training isn't landing as hard as you thought it was.

industry-news.title: Apple’s £3B iCloud Lawsuit Could Affect 40M UK Users
industry-news.excerpt: Apple lost a bid to narrow a UK iCloud lawsuit from Which?, keeping a £3 billion competition claim on track for an October 2028 trial. The post Apple’s £3B iCloud Lawsuit Could Affect 40M UK Users app
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple failed to get a UK court to dismiss a £3 billion lawsuit from consumer group Which?, meaning the case will proceed to trial in October 2028 with potential implications for 40 million UK iCloud users. This matters to digital workplace pros because it's a bellwether for how regulators are scrutinizing cloud storage practices around data, pricing, and consumer choice. Honestly, when your legal team can't kill a case at summary judgment, you're probably looking at years of discovery that'll make your compliance team's hair turn white.

industry-news.title: LastPass Confirms Vendor Breach Exposed Customer Contact, Support Data
industry-news.excerpt: LastPass said customer contact and support data were exposed after attackers used stolen Klue OAuth tokens to access its Salesforce environment and CRM records. The post LastPass Confirms Vendor Breac
industry-news.dwp_take: LastPass confirmed that attackers used stolen OAuth tokens to break into their Salesforce environment and grab customer contact and support data from their CRM. This matters because most of your workforce is probably using LastPass for password management, which means your people's information just got compromised along with thousands of others. Here's the thing: if a password manager gets breached through their own vendor's security theater, it's a reminder that no tool is a magic bullet and you still need proper access controls and monitoring.
